entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sophia of Bavaria (1105–1145) was a German noblewoman and nun.

 Born into the powerful House of Zähringen, Sophia was married twice, first to Duke Frederick III of Upper Lorraine and then to Duke Henry V of Zähringen, making her Duchess of Zähringen and Margravine of Styria.

 Sophia's life was marked by her religious devotion and her role as a patron of the arts, supporting the construction of several churches and monasteries throughout her territories.

 Her legacy extends beyond her own lifetime, as she played a key role in shaping the medieval German nobility and influencing the political landscape of the Holy Roman Empire.

 As a testament to her enduring legacy, Sophia's descendants continued to play important roles in European politics for centuries to come, leaving behind a lasting impact on the course of history.

 In the annals of medieval history, Sophia of Bavaria stands as a testament to the power of women in shaping the destiny of nations.
